clue.text: Indian cookery with its origin at sea

parts.note: balti is a style of Indian cooking served in a wok-like pot, so the word stands for the cuisine

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, so only the opening letter of cookery is taken

explanation.surface: A remark that curry-making was first practised on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria lets 'Indian cookery' read as one phrase: BALTI is the Indian dish, and the opening letter of 'cookery' (its origin) gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic is the sea bordered by Scandinavia, Germany, Poland and the Baltic states.

clue.text: Relative's 'abitual resort

indicators.note: the dropped h in the spelling tells us to drop the H, Cockney style, from the habitual resort

parts.note: a haunt is a habitual resort, a place one frequents

explanation.surface: A remark that a relation always goes to the same old holiday spot, in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: A haunt is a 'habitual resort'; the apostrophe in ''abitual' shows the H dropped, leaving AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a family member, the sister of a parent, so she is a relative.

clue.text: Tree from tree — throw away the incomplete

indicators.note: the second tree's letters are rearranged, the new word being made from them

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away

indicators.note: the word the is left unfinished, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to make one tree out of another by discarding the half-finished parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'tree' does double service as definition and as fodder for 'from', the anagram signal; 'incomplete' cuts the last letter from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: The terebinth is a Mediterranean tree of the pistachio family, a source of turpentine.

clue.text: Funny thing, fishy perhaps, about Araucaria

indicators.note: the fishy word goes around the setter, enclosing him

parts.note: a jokey adjective from cod, meaning like a cod, so fishy in a playful sense
the setter refers to himself, so his name stands for me

explanation.surface: The setter describes himself as a comic figure with something fishy about him.
explanation.walkthrough: The fishy word is a jokey coinage from cod, hence 'perhaps'; 'about' signals the wrap, and setters commonly refer to themselves by their pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedy is a humorous play or show, something meant to be funny; it is also the theme play here.

clue.text: Money heard to support GI

parts.note: dough is slang for money

indicators.note: the word for support is said aloud, and its sound gives the letters

parts.note: a buoy keeps something afloat, supporting it in water

explanation.surface: Cash is said to have been raised to back an American soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' signals a sound-alike: the float that supports something is pronounced the same as the word for a lad in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Doughboy was the nickname for an American infantryman in the First World War, a forerunner of GI.

clue.text: I hoped foursomes would be played in the 4 of 19

indicators.note: the letters of the golfing words would be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer's hope that fourball matches would be staged during a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4 of 19 is COMEDY of ERRORS, Shakespeare's play; the fodder I HOPED FOURSOMES rearranges to name one of its twin servants.
explanation.definitionFit: Dromio of Ephesus is one of the twin servants in Shakespeare's The Comedy of Errors.

clue.text: A French bearing in a fantastic youth leader is awkward

parts.note: un is the French word for a

indicators.note: the compass bearing is placed inside the word for fantastic

parts.note: wild can mean fantastic, extravagant or far-fetched
a compass bearing such as east, abbreviated E

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A clumsy Frenchman carrying a weird scout leader around.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' before 'fantastic' and 'is' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwieldy describes something hard to handle because of its size or shape, so it is awkward.

clue.text: Believer's timeless crime

indicators.note: without time, T being the physics abbreviation for time

parts.note: a theist is a believer in God; the possessive adds no letters

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a person of faith committed an ageless offence.
explanation.definitionFit: A heist is a robbery, especially a large, planned one, and so a crime.

clue.text: See 12
Protected by French painter cut short on the road to love

indicators.note: the painter's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French painter
the M1 motorway, written MI in crosswords, is the main road north from London
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone shielded by a French artist on the way to romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the road to love' places MI before O.
explanation.definitionFit: In gremio is Latin for in the bosom, used of something held in safe keeping, so protected.

clue.text: Reason to hold one hand? No real reason

indicators.note: the word for reason holds the others inside it

parts.note: why means reason, as in the whys and wherefores
the Roman numeral for one is I
hand means handwriting, hence MS for manuscript

explanation.surface: Asking why someone should grip a single hand, and concluding there is no good reason.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsy is a passing fancy or impulse, acting on a whim rather than from a real reason.

clue.text: Early, about the start of day, Conservative is the last thing one wants to hear

definitions.text: the last thing one wants to hear

indicators.note: the word for early goes around the next letter

parts.note: betimes is an old word for early

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Grumbling that an early-morning Tory is something no one wants to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last thing one wants to hear' sounds like a complaint, but it really means the story heard last thing at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A child is read a story at bedtime, the final thing heard before sleep, a witty twist on the idiom.

clue.text: An end to vacation (American father's, say), charge mostly interchangeable with 5 down

parts.note: a tip is an end, as in the tip of the tongue
hol is short for holiday, a vacation

indicators.note: say means the words are spoken, and their sound gives the letters

parts.note: father's can be read as belonging to a sire, of sire

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, one letter being dropped

parts.note: to charge someone is to accuse them

explanation.surface: A rambling note on finishing a holiday and an American dad's charges, compared with a stage character.
explanation.walkthrough: OF SIRE is said like OF SYR; 'mostly' drops one C from ACCUSE. In the play, Dromio of Ephesus repeatedly mistakes Antipholus of Syracuse for his own master.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipholus of Syracuse is mistaken by Dromio of Ephesus for his own master, so the two get muddled in the play.

clue.text: A negative before long

parts.note: non is a negative prefix and the French for no

explanation.surface: A refusal ahead of something lengthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for soon or shortly, meaning in a little while.

clue.text: Historic family past its sell-by date?

definitions.meaning: a family of long-established lineage, of ancient descent
goods kept on the shelves too long, stale merchandise

explanation.surface: A grand ancestral line wonders whether it has gone stale.
explanation.definitionFit: Old stock means both a long-established family line and stale goods kept too long.

clue.text: It lights up to take Mrs Blair when one's in the wrong place

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

indicators.note: the letter standing for one sits out of its usual spot in the name

parts.note: Cherie Blair is the wife of former UK prime minister Tony Blair

explanation.surface: Something bright collects the prime minister's wife after she arrives at the wrong venue.
explanation.walkthrough: CHERIE becomes CHIERE with its I (one) shifted.
explanation.definitionFit: A torchiere is a tall floor lamp directing light upwards, so it lights up the ceiling.

clue.text: Picture the thing left by painter first

indicators.note: first says the left and painter pieces come before the thing

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter
it means the thing

explanation.surface: An artist leaves something behind as their first act.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painted or photographed likeness of a person, a kind of picture.

clue.text: With "Is he good at heart?" comes a thought of merriment

indicators.note: the French word for good goes into the heart of he

parts.note: bon is French for good

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a man is truly kind brings a cheerful idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic paraphrase of merrythought, the old name for the forked bone of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Merrythought is the traditional name for the forked breastbone of a fowl, pulled for luck.

clue.text: Stood with unaffected scent

definitions.meaning: a flower that would smell as sweet by any other name, in Shakespeare's line

explanation.surface: Someone stood up wearing a plain natural perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: Juliet says a rose by any other name would smell as sweet: its scent is unaffected by what it is called.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the past tense of rise, and also the flower whose fragrance a change of name cannot alter.

clue.text: Fears receiving capital punishment for mistakes

indicators.note: being beheaded, so the word for fears loses its first letter

parts.note: terrors are great fears

explanation.surface: Frightening executions are carried out for blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital punishment here is beheading, taking off the head letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Errors are mistakes; the word also completes the theme play's title.

clue.text: The House on the South Island

definitions.meaning: ..., the Oxford college, is known to its members as the House
the largest city of New Zealand's South Island

explanation.surface: A building located on an island in the southern hemisphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ Church is the Oxford college called the House, and Christchurch is New Zealand's South Island city.

clue.text: See 22
Scottish theologian lacking intelligence over destination of wood

indicators.note: in a down entry the theologian sits over, above, the next piece

parts.note: John Duns Scotus was a medieval Scottish theologian
inane means silly, lacking sense

explanation.surface: A Scottish scholar is dismissed as stupid over where a forest ended up.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth, the witches say he is safe until Birnam Wood comes to Dunsinane, which it does.
explanation.definitionFit: Birnam Wood moves to Dunsinane Hill in Macbeth, so that hill is the wood's destination.

clue.text: One getting about on a mountain camel

indicators.note: in an across entry one piece sits on another by following it

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
a means one
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A single animal travelling around on a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American member of the camel family, related to the llama.

clue.text: Discover Pole detailed to keep 26, maybe

indicators.note: the shortened pole keeps the donkey inside it
de-tailed, losing the last letter

parts.note: the South Pole
26 is a she-ass, and a moke is slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: A Polish man is assigned to look after a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a person from Poland, but it is the South Pole; SOUT keeps MOKE.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoke out is to force something hidden into the open, to discover or expose it.

clue.text: When optimum and maximum could be dangerous?

definitions.text: When optimum and maximum could be dangerous?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
best means optimum
OS stands for outsize, the maximum size of clothing

explanation.surface: A question about when the best and the biggest might be hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue hints at the material: harmless at best, dangerous in quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral whose dust is a known health hazard.

clue.text: Hinny's mummy's incongruous sashes

indicators.note: out of place, so the letters of sashes are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A mule-like animal's mother wears ill-matched sashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinny is the offspring of a stallion and a female donkey, so its mother is a female donkey.
